transcript.text: Just had a new induction hob fitted, Beko. When I put my saucepan on it just flashes a U and doesn't heat. Is it faulty? It's brand new!!

Probably not faulty. A flashing U on a Beko induction hob means "no suitable pan detected". The hob is working: it's looking for a pan it can heat and not finding one, so it won't switch the zone on. Induction only heats magnetic (iron-based) cookware that sits flat and is big enough for the zone. The most likely causes, in order: 1. The saucepan isn't induction-compatible. Aluminium, copper, glass and some stainless steel pans just won't register. This is by far the most common reason with a newly fitted hob.
2. The pan is too small for the zone, off-centre, or has a domed or warped base, so the hob can't sense it properly.
3. Much less likely: a fault in that zone's coil or power module. Quick checks to tell these apart: 1. Hold a fridge magnet to the base of the pan. If it sticks firmly, the pan is suitable. If it doesn't stick or only barely clings, the pan isn't induction-compatible, and that's your answer: no fault with the hob. Many pans have an induction symbol (a coil-like zigzag) underneath.
2. If the magnet sticks, put the pan centrally on a zone that roughly matches its base size, with a little water in it, and switch on. A small pan on a large zone can fail to register.
3. Try the same magnetic pan on the other zones. If it heats on the others but one zone keeps flashing U, that points to that zone's coil or power module. As the hob is brand new, that would be a warranty job for Beko or your installer, not something to open up. If no magnetic, right-sized pan works on any zone, contact Beko under the warranty. Do let me know what the magnet test shows, though, as I'd expect it to solve this.
Tried the magnet! It doesn't stick to the saucepans, but it does stick to my cast-iron casserole, and that heated up fine. So is it just my pans?

Yes, it's probably just your saucepans. If a magnet won't stick to the base, the induction hob can't detect or heat the pan, and the flashing U is it telling you exactly that. The casserole heating up fine shows the hob is working as it should. That's normal induction behaviour, not a fault. 1. Put the casserole, with a little water in it, on each zone in turn and switch it on for a few seconds. If every zone heats, the hob is fine.
2. If one zone still flashes U even with the casserole on it, that would point to that zone's coil or power module. Report that to Beko or your installer under the warranty rather than opening anything up. 1. Replace the saucepans with induction-compatible ones. Look for the coil symbol underneath, or take a fridge magnet shopping: it should stick firmly to the base. 2. If there are pans you really want to keep, an induction converter disc lets non-magnetic pans work. It heats more slowly and less efficiently, though, so it's best for occasional use. If a pan the magnet sticks to firmly still won't register on any zone, that's when it's worth calling Beko.

candidates: Saucepan not induction-compatible (non-magnetic base, e.g. aluminium, copper or some stainless steel) (high)
Pan too small for the zone, or base warped/not sitting flat or centred (medium)
Zone coil or power (generator) module fault (low)

reading.symptom: flashes U and doesn't heat with saucepan on

plan: They asked: "Is it faulty?" - answer that first.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Beko; code U.
The fault they reported is: "flashes U and doesn't heat with saucepan on". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.

claimsRejected.claim: A flat base that roughly matches the zone size works best.

candidates: Fault in a single zone's coil or power module (low)

plan: They asked: "Is it just my pans?" - answer that first.

Checks they have done and what they found: magnet test on saucepans - magnet doesn't stick; magnet test and heating with cast-iron casserole - magnet sticks and casserole heated up fine.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Beko; code U.
The fault they reported is: "flashes U and doesn't heat with saucepan on". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 2: the checks they reported did not fix it. Give the next check that best separates the remaining likely causes, or say what the likely faulty part is if the checks already point to one. Until a check has confirmed which part has failed, name it as the likely part and the check that would confirm it; do not tell them to buy, order or replace it.
